C2_calibration.ruling: yes, C2 needs a written clarification for P2 (and for lit lamps in P1); not a looser threshold
proposed_rule: H (house) elements are not matches: for P2, the transparent background, the house light (key camera-left 45/30, fill right, 5000K), the house framing (80% of the limiting dimension, centred, 4:5) and the category's house angle (2.3 table, written 2026-11-11). They count as H only when the image measurably follows the spec (fill 80% +-3%, centre +-2%, alpha 0 outside the product, key side camera-left, angle per the table).

A component counts as a match only when (a) our image departs from the house spec toward the supplier's choice (example: the lamp P2 under-view of the lens), or (b) the supplier's choice is distinctive and ours repeats it: a coloured or textured backdrop, a surface with a horizon, a hard cast shadow, coloured or back light, the lamp switched on, an off-centre or cropped framing, a tilt or an unusual camera height.
(5) styling is unchanged; in P2 it is the arrangement (fold, grouping, spacing, orientation); never in textiles.

New C2b, no traced surface: high-pass luminance NCC inside the product after bbox alignment, against every supplier image of the same SKU; pass when the zero-offset value is at most the largest shifted/mirrored control + 0.10 and below 0.15 absolute (pilot: vase 0.00-0.01 vs controls -0.02..+0.02). The silhouette must match (that is fidelity) and is not scored.

P2 passes with at most 2 counted matches plus C2b. P1 keeps the current wording, with one clarification: a lamp's own lit pattern (its beams) counts under (4) only when the ambient light (direction, colour, character) matches too.
